references.text: The Lord makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel by protecting the land of Goshen from swarms of flies, demonstrating the same principle that God separates His people from the Egyptians.
The Lord distinguishes between the livestock of Israel and that of Egypt, with none of the Israelites' animals dying - the same theme of God's protection and separation.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, did no hail fall - yet another example of God making a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
All the Israelites had light where they lived while Egypt was in darkness, illustrating God's separation between the two peoples.
The blood on the doorposts protects the Israelites from the destroyer - the concrete fulfillment of God's promise to separate Israel from Egypt.
Not a dog moved its tongue against the children of Israel - the same expression (לֹא יֶחֱרַץ־כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ) showing God's complete protection of His people.
The Lord has set apart His holy ones for Himself - the theme that God sets apart and protects His people.
Dogs that cannot bark - a contrast to the dogs in Exodus that did not even lift their tongues against Israel.
Both verses confirm that Israel's security is guaranteed by God's protection against any hostile power.
